title: Virtual Environment Setup for OSINT
description: Set up a safe and isolated virtual environment for OSINT investigations. Using a VM protects your real identity and keeps your host system clean.

sections.title: Why Use a Virtual Machine?
sections.description: A Virtual Machine (VM) is a software-based computer that runs inside your real computer. For OSINT work, a VM provides isolation — your investigation activity stays inside the VM and does not affect your host system.
topics: Your real IP and identity stays protected
Malicious files opened inside VM cannot harm your host
You can take snapshots and revert to a clean state anytime
Separate browser profiles and accounts inside VM
Easy to reset — delete VM and start fresh
sections.note: Never do OSINT investigations directly from your main system. Always use an isolated environment.

sections.title: VM Software Options
sections.description: Choose one of these VM platforms to create your isolated OSINT environment.

tools.name: VirtualBox
tools.description: Free and open-source. Best choice for beginners. Supports Windows, Linux, macOS. Install Kali Linux or Ubuntu inside it.

tools.name: VMware Workstation Player
tools.description: Free for personal use. More stable performance than VirtualBox on some systems. Good for running Kali Linux.

sections.title: Setting Up Kali Linux in VM
sections.description: Kali Linux is the recommended OS for OSINT and security investigations. It comes pre-installed with many useful tools.
topics: Download Kali Linux VM image from official site (kali.org)
Import the .ova file into VirtualBox or VMware
Take a snapshot before installing any tools

commands.cmd: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
commands.description: Update all packages after first boot. Always do this before installing anything.

commands.cmd: sudo apt install git curl wget -y
commands.description: Install basic tools needed for downloading and running OSINT scripts.
Install Tor browser for anonymous browsing during investigations.

sections.title: VM Network Configuration
sections.description: Proper network configuration is critical. Wrong settings can expose your real IP during investigations.
topics: NAT mode — VM shares host IP (default, basic protection)
Host-only mode — VM has no internet access (safe for offline analysis)
Bridged mode — VM gets its own IP (avoid for OSINT)
Use NAT + VPN inside VM for best protection
sections.note: Always use NAT network mode. Never use Bridged mode during OSINT — it exposes your real network.

commands.description: Check your current public IP inside the VM. Verify VPN is working before starting any investigation.
Show all network interfaces and IP addresses inside the VM.

sections.title: Snapshots — Clean State
sections.description: Snapshots let you save the current state of your VM and revert back to it anytime. Take a clean snapshot before every investigation.
topics: After investigation: revert to clean snapshot
This removes all traces of your investigation activity

commands.description: Take a snapshot via command line in VirtualBox. Replace VM Name with your VM name.
Restore VM to clean snapshot state via command line.

sections.title: Essential OSINT Tools Installation
sections.description: Install these tools inside your VM after taking a clean snapshot.

tools.description: Gather emails, subdomains, IPs from public sources. Pre-installed in Kali Linux.

tools.name: Maltego CE
tools.description: Visual link analysis tool. Free community edition available. Great for mapping relationships.
